sections.html:
Along the Appomattox River, around 21 miles below Richmond, Petersburg stands at the fall line where the Piedmont meets the coastal plain. The independent city spans some 23 square miles. Its population was 33,458 in 2020 and is estimated at 33,734 for 2025.

Housing data from 2020 shows 15,382 households and 18,013 housing units, with 14.6% of those units vacant. Dinwiddie and Prince George counties wrap around the city, but Petersburg has no county government of its own above it. One set of city departments handles assessment, tax bills, code enforcement and permits.

Because two interstates cross here, many owners live close to jobs in Richmond, Colonial Heights, Hopewell and the Fort Lee area.

Age defines a lot of Petersburg housing. The town incorporated in 1748, rebuilt after a big fire in 1815, and took heavy damage during the siege of 1864 and 1865. Tobacco, cotton, flour, iron and railroads fed later growth and left behind brick rowhouses, mill-era housing and big Victorian homes. Inside, expect original plaster, dated wiring and tired plumbing.

  • The Old Town Historic District covers about 190 acres and was placed on the National Register of Historic Places on July 4, 1980.
  • Pocahontas Island, among the oldest free Black settlements in the state, is its own historic district.
  • Battersea, a Palladian house built in 1767 and 1768, overlooks the river from the city's western edge.

Houses inside a historic area can face extra review for repairs and exterior changes. Owners of worn older homes often prefer a buyer who takes the place without a to-do list.

Hot, muggy summers and cool winters are normal. Rain or snow totals about 47 inches in a year, falling on roughly 115 days. That steady moisture is hard on old roofs, wood trim, crawl spaces and basements. If a house has sat empty through a few humid seasons, look for leaks and mold before you choose how to sell.

Lots low on the Appomattox deserve a flood map check before listing. The city can tell you about your own parcel.

Under City Code Sec. 22-140, an owner whose building has stood continuously vacant for 12 months or more must register it with the building code official. Occasional use during that stretch does not break the vacancy.

  • Registering the first time costs $100. After that, $100 more, non-refundable, is due within 15 days of each anniversary for as long as the building is empty.
  • Filers supply the address, owner and agent contacts, an estimate of how long the building will stay empty and a maintenance plan.
  • Owners must also show an ongoing rodent control plan for the inside and outside.
  • Failing to register is a civil violation carrying a $200 penalty. The penalty is $400 in a historic area, a conservation or rehabilitation district, or an area that council has declared blighted.

A notice is mailed at least 30 days ahead of any penalty. Reach the Housing Inspector at 106 W. Tabb St. or 804-733-2410, weekdays from 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. For a house you inherited or no longer use, the fees keep recurring, and selling stops them.

The city looks at every real estate assessment once every two years, measuring value as of January 1. The market, changes to a property and corrections can push a value up, down or nowhere. Bills from the next July 1 through June 30 are based on that January 1 figure.

Notices of changed assessments are mailed on January 28 of a reassessment year, and only owners whose value moved receive one. Appeals start with an office review and can go on to the Board of Review. Family transfers, foreclosures, bank sales and estate sales can be excluded from the sales analysis, since they are not arm's-length deals.

Selling mid-year? The closing agent can explain how the current bill is handled at settlement. More detail is on the city's Assessment page.

Petersburg started as a manufacturing and rail town, and a few of those companies are still here, including Arnold Pen Co., Seward Trunk Co., Titmus Optical and Amsted Rail-Brenco. Much of today's hiring happens right beyond the city line, where Dinwiddie County has a Walmart distribution center and an Amazon fulfillment center, and Fort Lee is another big employer nearby.

Interstates 95 and 85 come together in the city, the south end of I-295 is just south of it, and US 1, US 301 and US 460 all pass through. CSX and Norfolk Southern both run rail operations here. Richmond International Airport is less than 30 miles north. That draws buyers from different directions: commuters bound for Richmond, workers at the distribution centers and base, and investors ready to renovate older stock. Point out the highway and rail access when you describe the house.

sections.h2: What does a seller pay at closing in Petersburg?
sections.html:
The state levies a grantor tax of 50 cents on every $500 of the price. By default the seller owes it, though the parties can agree that the buyer picks up part or all. A deed is not recorded until the clerk certifies payment, and the money is split between the state and the locality. Read the statute at Virginia Code 58.1-802.

Remaining closing costs vary with the type of sale. Get an itemized estimate from your closing company before picking a route, because listing and repairing can net very differently than selling as is for cash.

sections.h2: How a cash sale works in Petersburg
sections.html:
Start by telling us about the house, its condition and when you need to move. After we review it, any offer reflects the property in its current state, with no repairs or cleanout from you. Saying no is always fine and costs nothing.

  • Pull together your deed, current tax bill, payoff letters and any vacancy registration papers.
  • Choose a closing company for the title search.
  • Agree on a closing day that fits your plans.
  • Sign, take your proceeds and pass along the keys.

Back taxes and fees are taken from the proceeds at the table, so nothing is due beforehand. When comparing choices, line up a traditional listing, an investor sale and a cash offer on net proceeds, time to close and repairs you would pay for first.

The typical seller owns a house that is old, empty or inherited. Put-off repairs, a vacancy registration due for renewal, back taxes and scattered heirs come up again and again. Cash works best when the problem is time or condition.

faqs.q: How many people live in Petersburg, VA?
faqs.a: Estimates put the 2025 population at 33,734, a little above the 33,458 counted in 2020.

faqs.q: Does Petersburg have a vacant property registry?
faqs.a: Yes. Owners of buildings empty for 12 months or more register them with the building code official and pay $100 a year. Skipping it costs $200, or $400 in historic or blighted areas.

faqs.q: How often does Petersburg reassess real estate?
faqs.a: Once every two years, based on January 1 values. Owners whose value changed get notices on January 28 of that year.

faqs.q: When are Petersburg real estate taxes due?
faqs.a: Four installments fall on September 30, December 31, March 30 and June 30 within each July-to-June billing year.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Petersburg house that needs major repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. Cash buyers take houses as is, so repairs and cleanouts are not required beforehand.
